transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Nice to meet you too. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my wife thinks I'm not eating enough. I mean, most days I just have some coffee and a piece of toast in the morning, and then maybe a little soup or some vegetables later on. Big meals just feel unnecessary at my age, to be honest.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, my mood is fine. I haven't been feeling depressed or anything like that. I just... well, I just don't have much interest in eating a whole lot. But my spirits are perfectly okay.
Have you been having problems with your memory?
No, I haven't noticed any problems there. I mean, I remember things just fine. My mind is still perfectly sharp, so... no, no issues with my memory.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Yes, to be honest, I am. When my wife tries to put butter on things, or if she serves me a full plate for dinner... well, I get nervous. I just worry that I'll start putting weight back on and lose the control I've worked so hard to keep. So, yes, I do worry about that.
Do you see yourself as overweight?

Well, I don't know if I'd use the word overweight, exactly. But I do pay close attention to my shape. 

Like... if my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It's a good feeling. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, well, I just feel sloppy. I get really disappointed in myself. So I guess I do judge myself pretty hard on how my stomach looks.
Have you lost a lot of weight recently?

Well, yes, I suppose I have. My regular doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low lately. But to be honest with you, I don't see the problem. To me, being lighter just makes it a lot easier to get around out in the garden and keep up on my daily walks. So I think it's actually been quite helpful.
Has your weight dropped so low that a doctor has told you that you are underweight?

Well, I'm not sure if he used that exact word. Like I just mentioned, he mostly just told me the number on the scale was getting too low for a fella my age. He didn't give me an official label or say I was officially underweight or anything like that. Just that he was concerned about the number being lower than he'd like.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don't do anything like that. I just watch what I eat and try to stay active. I've never made myself throw up.
Has your doctor told you your weight is dangerously low for your height?

No, he didn't use the word dangerous. Like I mentioned a minute ago, he just looked at my chart and said the number was lower than he'd like. But he never made it sound like it was some kind of emergency, or dangerously low for my height, no.
Do you know your current height and weight?

I'm around five foot nine. But as for my weight... I honestly don't know the exact number right now. I don't keep a scale at the house, and I didn't really look too closely when the doctor weighed me the other day.
Do you believe you are still too heavy, even though your doctor is concerned that your weight is low?

Well, I don't know if I'd say I'm too heavy, but... I just don't really see why everyone is making such a big fuss about my weight. Older folks are supposed to eat less anyway, right? It's just natural. I'm still managing all my chores around the house, and I'm still taking my daily tours around the neighborhood just fine. So I really don't get what the concern is all about.
Has a doctor ever told you that your body weight is significantly below what is healthy for your height?

Well, like I was just saying, my doctor did tell me that the number on the scale has gotten too low. But honestly, to me, being a bit lighter just makes it easier to get around the garden and keep up on my walks.
Do you feel fat even when other people tell you that you are too thin?

I wouldn't use the word "fat," exactly. It's more about... well, just keeping myself in check. Like, if my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself, you know? Kept things tidy. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, I just feel sloppy. It's disappointing. I just want to stay trim.
Do you know whether your doctor has said your weight is below 85 percent of what would be expected for your height?
I don't think he ever used those exact numbers. He just said I was underweight and needed to be careful. I don't remember anything about 85 percent, though.
Do you ever use laxatives, diet pills, or anything else to keep yourself from gaining weight?

No, I don't take anything like that. No diet pills, and... well, I'd only ever use a laxative if I was actually backed up, but certainly not to keep my weight down. I don't mess with any of that stuff. I just manage things myself by watching my portions and staying active.
What is your current weight?

I don't remember the exact number from my last appointment, to be honest. I just know my regular doctor says the number on the scale has gotten too low. But... well, to me, being lighter just makes it easier to get around the garden. It helps me keep up on my walks without feeling weighed down, so I think it's fine.
Have you noticed a drop in your sexual interest lately?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. I mean, I'm 78 years old, so it's not exactly a big part of my life anymore anyway. But no, there hasn't been any sudden drop or change recently.
Before menopause, did your periods ever stop for a time when your weight was low?
Well, doctor, I'm a man. So... no, I've never had periods, and I certainly didn't go through menopause. I think you might have your questions mixed up there.
Has your doctor specifically told you that you are underweight?

Well, like I mentioned a couple of minutes ago, yes, he did. My regular doctor told me the number on the scale has gotten too low. But I just don't see it as a bad thing. Being lighter makes it a lot easier for me to get around the garden and keep up on my daily walks without feeling so weighed down. So he might say I'm too light, but to me, it just makes moving around easier.
Has your doctor told you that your weight is significantly below what is considered healthy for your height?

Well, like I just mentioned a moment ago, he did say my weight was too low. But he didn't use those exact words... he didn't say it was significantly below what's healthy for my height, or give me any kind of chart or anything. He just pointed out that I was underweight. That's really all he said about it.
